issues.legal_issue: A civil decree for partition and possession is not null merely because persons claiming tenancy rights were joined as defendants where the civil court was competent to determine the title dispute and the claimed tenancy rights were not established.
material_facts: A suit for partition and possession involving title was brought against the persons claiming to be tenants, who were joined as defendants.

The claimed tenants did not participate in the suit by presenting evidence, and the trial court found that they had not established personal cultivation, payment of rent, or a continuing landlord-tenant relationship.
The decree was passed before the later tenancy legislation on which the claim to ownership relied came into force.
The trial court found that the tenancy legislation then applicable did not prevent the civil court from deciding the partition and possession suit.
issues.conclusion: The decree was not a nullity, the civil court had jurisdiction to pass it, and the claimed tenants were not entitled to a declaration of ownership under the later tenancy legislation.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the scheme of the Bombay Tenancy Act, 1939, concluding that it did not bar a civil court from deciding a suit for partition and possession involving title. Because the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 came into force after the possession suit was instituted, execution of the decree by the ordinary civil court was permissible. The claimed ownership under Section 32 of the 1948 Act was not established on the findings that the claimants had not proved the required tenancy and cultivation facts. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: suit_involves_title_and_possession and claimed_tenants_were_parties and (tenancy_status_not_established or later_tenancy_law_postdates_suit)

predicates.suit_involves_title_and_possession: The proceeding sought partition or recovery of possession and required the court to determine rights in the property.
predicates.claimed_tenants_were_parties: Persons asserting tenancy rights were joined as parties to the property suit.
predicates.tenancy_status_not_established: The persons asserting tenancy rights did not establish the facts supporting their claimed tenancy, such as personal cultivation or payment of rent.
predicates.later_tenancy_law_postdates_suit: The tenancy law relied on for a later ownership claim came into force after the property suit was instituted.

issues.definition: When a property suit involving title and possession includes the persons asserting tenancy rights, and their tenancy is not established or the relied-on tenancy law postdates the suit, the decree is not void and those persons do not acquire ownership under that later law.

issues.legal_issue: Actual possession may be delivered in execution of a valid decree for possession when the persons resisting execution have not established a right to remain in possession.
material_facts: The decree directed recovery of possession from the defendants, including the persons later resisting actual delivery.
After symbolic possession had been delivered, the decree-holder sought actual possession.
The executing court ordered actual possession to be delivered after hearing the parties.
The claimed tenants had not established that they remained in possession as tenants, and the underlying decree was not a nullity.
issues.conclusion: The order directing delivery of actual physical possession in execution of the decree was justified.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Code of Civil Procedure, including the execution framework invoked through Section 47, a lawful decree for possession may be executed by delivery of actual possession. The Court relied on its conclusion that the decree was not void and that the resisting claimants had not established a tenancy-based right to possession. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: execution_proceeding and valid_possession_decree and decree_covers_resisting_occupants and tenancy_right_not_established

predicates.execution_proceeding: The court is considering how to enforce an existing judgment or decree.
predicates.valid_possession_decree: A court with authority made an effective decree requiring possession to be delivered.
predicates.decree_covers_resisting_occupants: The possession decree applies to the persons resisting delivery of the property.
predicates.tenancy_right_not_established: The persons resisting delivery did not establish a tenancy-based right to remain in possession.

issues.definition: In an execution proceeding, actual possession may be delivered when an effective possession decree covers the resisting occupants and they have not established a tenancy-based right to stay.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal by special leave does not ordinarily warrant reappraisal of factual or legal conclusions unless a serious error causing injustice is shown.
material_facts: The courts below found that the claimants had not proved the asserted tenancy or personal cultivation and that the possession decree was not a nullity.
The Supreme Court found no misreading of evidence, serious misunderstanding of its effect, or disregard of important evidence that would fundamentally affect the result.
The challenged judgments were not shown to contain a serious legal infirmity resulting in grave injustice.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to reappraise the evidence or disturb the conclusions below and dismissed both appeals.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied its settled practice in appeals by special leave: it does not ordinarily reconsider all factual or legal conclusions reached below, but may examine the evidence in rare cases involving misreading, serious misunderstanding, or complete disregard of important evidence that causes injustice. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal and lower_court_findings_challenged and not serious_error_causing_injustice_shown

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal brought by special leave.
predicates.lower_court_findings_challenged: The appellant asks the reviewing court to reconsider factual or legal conclusions reached by the courts below.
predicates.serious_error_causing_injustice_shown: The appellant establishes a serious evidentiary or legal error that caused injustice.

issues.definition: In an appeal by special leave challenging lower-court findings, those findings are not reappraised or disturbed unless a serious error causing injustice is shown.
